definition.proposition: Near-duplicate removal in the training corpus helps by itself: at matched document count (698,714 docs), E1 trained on deduplicated code-py-v2 reaches 1.6% lower clean80 bpc than E1 on an undeduplicated uniform v1 subset (code-py-v1sub); the remaining coverage/size effect (v1 vs v1sub) is +0.6%.

scope.dataset: code-py-v2 vs code-py-v1sub vs code-py-v1; clean80 doc-level bpc on v1 val

definition.refutation_criteria: With >= 4 seeds the paired v1sub-vs-v2 gap's 95% CI includes 0, or the gap is below 1.0%

qual: 4 seeds; LR tuned on v1 (K7) used for all arms
reason: D1 PASS: D (v1sub vs v2) = +1.62%, paired 95% CI [+0.92%, +2.31%], df 3, per seed +1.89/+1.77/+0.97/+1.84%. D2 PASS: S (v1 vs v1sub) = +0.64% (approx CI [+0.16%, +1.12%]). D3: D + S = +2.27% vs the H5 gap +3.08% (single-seed H5). Registered rule: A3 v2 results stand as 'with dedup'.

limitations.text: One architecture (E1) and one LR (6e-3, tuned on v1 by K7, applied to all three corpora); 200M tokens only

verified_at.basis: HEAD of the checkout when the event was recorded
